strategy.summary: Reproduce numpy PR 29372: np.unique with equal_nan=True on a 1D array containing NaNs should collapse NaNs. Build numpy from the buggy commit bde097d548a1, then run the two 1D axis tests added by the PR. They should fail there (NaNs not collapsed on the axis path) and pass on the PR head (1D input with axis=0/-1 dispatches to the axis=None _unique1d path). The 2D axis=0 case is explicitly unfixed and is not used. Python and numpy versions are not stated in the evidence, so they are left unpinned and the choice is flagged in risks.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy.git numpy && cd numpy && git checkout bde097d548a1 && git submodule update --init
python -m pip install -r requirements/build_requirements.txt || python -m pip install meson-python ninja Cython
pinned_because: pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md as test dependencies, but no version constraint is stated, so they are unpinned.
numpy has no documented or era-table constraint; the buggy revision is built from source so the installed numpy is the one under test.
Build tools (meson-python, ninja, Cython) are inferred from the numpy build system and are not stated in the evidence; they are era-inferred, not documented constraints.

strategy.reproducing_test: test_unique_axis0_equal_nan_on_1d_array and test_unique_axis_minus1_eq_on_1d_array in numpy/lib/tests/test_arraysetops.py, both calling np.unique on np.array([np.nan, 0, 0, np.nan]) with equal_nan=True and comparing to np.array([0., np.nan]) via assert_array_equal
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision bde097d548a1 both selected tests FAIL, because np.unique with axis=0 or axis=-1 on a 1D NaN-containing array returns an uncollapsed array whose shape differs from [0., nan], so assert_array_equal raises AssertionError. On the PR 29372 head both tests PASS, because 1D input is dispatched to the axis=None _unique1d path with equal_nan, which returns [0., nan] exactly.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; a=np.array([np.nan,0,0,np.nan]); print(np.unique(a,axis=0,equal_nan=True), np.unique(a,axis=-1,equal_nan=True))" (expected on fixed build: [ 0. nan] twice)

input_output_examples.buggy_output: NaNs not collapsed (exact buggy array not stated in evidence)

risks: Python and numpy versions are not stated; the build may fail on very new or very old Python. Pick the Python version the repo's pyproject requires at bde097d548a1.
Building numpy from source needs a working compiler and BLAS-free build; build time is long. Use an editable build to avoid repeated rebuilds.

test_unique_axis_float_raises_typeerror (axis=0.0 expecting TypeError 'integer argument expected') is not a fail-to-pass discriminator from the evidence: it may pass on both revisions. It is excluded from test_command and should be checked separately.
The 2D axis=0 NaN non-collapse is reported in the issue but explicitly NOT fixed by PR 29372, so do not use 2D inputs as a transition test.
The exact dispatch condition went through several iterations; the merged form is not confirmed in the passages. If the PR head differs from the described dispatch, the transition may not appear.
The 0 in the test array has no signed-zero discussion in the evidence; the expected value 0. is compared with assert_array_equal, which is exact, so only NaN placement matters here.
The test class name is not given in the diff context, so selection uses -k rather than a fully qualified node id.
The evidence's test_command (numpy.test()) is not a real pytest entry point for this purpose and is not relied upon.
No platform-specific behaviour is evidenced; NaN handling here is IEEE and should reproduce on Linux x86_64 with default flags. No sanitiser or special architecture is claimed by the evidence.

oracle.reference_source: expected values written in the PR test itself (np.array([0., np.nan]))
oracle.why: assert_array_equal compares exactly and treats NaNs at matching positions as equal; no tolerance is stated in the evidence.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On bde097d548a1 the axis=0/-1 path does not collapse NaNs, so the result has more than two elements or the wrong shape; assert_array_equal raises AssertionError against [0., nan]. The exact buggy array is not stated in the evidence.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR head the 1D input takes the axis=None _unique1d path with equal_nan=True, returning [0., nan] which matches the expected array, so both tests pass.
